newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania Bancorex bank posted lower '96 profit.
newsitem.headline: Romania Bancorex bank posted lower '96 profit.

text.p: Romania's large state-owned bank Banca Romana de Comert Exterior Bancorex SA posted a gross profit of 170 billion lei last year, down from 210 billion in 1995, the bank's annual report showed on Friday.
A bank official said the profit drop was partly due to larger provisions made in 1996 in a bid to "ensure a higher degree of coverage of lending portfolio".
As Bancorex paid no tax on its 1996 gross profit due to larger tax payments the previous year, its post-tax profit remained at gross profit level of 170 billion lei.

Total assets doubled from the previous year to 12.96 trillion lei at end-1996 as the bank, which handles a large part of Romania's foreign trade, expanded its product line and loan portfolio and opened new branches, the report said.
It said its loan portfolio rose by 30.7 percent in real terms to 8.59 trillion lei last year, of which 70 percent were loans in hard currency. The portfolio focused on investment projects.
But the share of overdue loans in total lending portfolio rose to 7.9 percent last year from 6.1 percent in 1995.
The report said the rise in overdue loans had been partly due to "an approach to some sectors which were not traditional for the bank, such as agriculture and real estate projects".
Bancorex has a share capital of 93.2 billion lei, unchanged from end-1995, while owners' equity rose to 814.7 billion lei at end-June from 726.2 billion lei in 1995.
The State Ownership Fund holds 62.27 percent of Bancorex share capital and investment companies have some 27 percent. The rest belongs to corporations and individuals.
Figures reported were according to Romanian accounting standards and were audited by Coopers & Lybrand.
The report also said the auditor's capital adequacy ratio at end-1996 was 8.3 percent, above the eight percent limit recomended by the Basle Committee.
